title: Incremental instrumentation roadmap and mini-experiments
content:
Purpose:
Lightweight playbook for doing small, measurable instrumentation changes (mini-experiments) rather than wide-sweeping telemetry projects. Goal: reduce probe/query cost and alert noise while preserving investigatability and SLO coverage. This doc is intentionally pragmatic: concrete experiments, minimal SQL/DSL sketches, what to measure and success criteria.

Scope / constraints:
- Focused on inference control plane + serving runtime surface (token-serving requests, routing, cache hits).
- Low-friction changes only: feature flags, sampling toggles, dashboard panel edits.
- Run experiments on a single tenant or synthetic probe group first. No org-wide rolling changes until success criteria met.
- Target reduction: 20-40% query cost per high-cardinality dashboard within 8 weeks for panels we touch.

Principles:
- Start small: change one sampling decision or one panel at a time.
- Measure before/after for 14-day windows (baseline vs treatment).
- Keep traces for high-severity flows; sample aggressively elsewhere.
- Make all changes reversible and behind named feature flags.
- Document owner & date on every change in the panel description.

Experiment catalogue (prioritized):
1) Prefix-KV cache probe reduction (2 weeks)
   - Hypothesis: we can reduce prefix cache probe traces from 100% to 10% for low-traffic tenants and still detect regressions.
   - Change: add sampling flag sample.kv_probe.default=0.1; sample.kv_probe.tenant_overrides=none initially.
   - Metrics to capture (pre/post): prefix_cache_probe_rate, cache_hit_ratio_by_tenant (p95/p50), tail_latency_token_ms (p99).
   - Tracing anchors: keep full spans when cache_hit=false; otherwise drop to sampled span with minimal annotations (tenant, model, seq_len).
   - Success: baseline error detection (example regressions seeded) reproduced at >=90% fidelity; query cost drop >=25%.

2) High-cardinality label rollup for slowest-query dashboard (3 weeks)
   - Hypothesis: replacing per-tenant panels with top-10 rollups + sampled tenant drilldowns reduces dashboard query cost by ~30% with minimal operator impact.
   - Change: create rollup panel: top10 by latency_cohort with pre-aggregated hourly buckets; remove the heavy per-tenant table from primary dashboard, keep a lightweight 'drilldown' button that runs an on-demand query (triggered by operator).
   - Metrics: dashboard_query_cost_hourly, avg_panel_render_time, operator_steps_to_investigate (manual audit).
   - Success: dashboard cost drop >=30%, mean operator time to get tenant context increases by <= 1 minute.

3) Adaptive trace-level sampling during auto-scaling spikes (3 weeks)
   - Hypothesis: temporarily increasing trace sampling during capacity scaling events gives better SRE diagnostics with bounded cost.
   - Change: sampling policy that sets sample.rate=1.0 for 10 minutes when node_autoscale_event=true; otherwise baseline sample.rate=0.05 for normal. Implement as a rule in tracing gateway.
   - Metrics: traces_per_minute, successful_root_cause_finds_during_incident, trace_storage_cost_ratio.
   - Success: incidents with autoscale involvement have useful traces >=80% of the time and overall trace ingestion cost grows <10% month-over-month.

4) Function-call/Tooling call flattening in spans (2 weeks)
   - Hypothesis: collapsing internal function-call microspans into a single annotated span for low-priority requests simplifies traces and lowers storage.
   - Change: add a span-collapser for non-errorful tool calls: create collapsed_span.kind="internal_compact" and add tags: tool_count, total_tool_ms. Keep detailed spans for error cases and for traffic where output_quality_drop>threshold.
   - Metrics: avg_spans_per_trace, median_trace_size_kb, trace-storage-cost.
   - Success: avg_spans_per_trace drops >=40% for sampled population; debugging fidelity unaffected in sampled error traces.

Instrumentation / metric definition notes (compact):
- prefix_cache_probe_rate: gauge per minute; unit=probes/min; tag: tenant, model_family. Baseline: 4-6 probes/min per active tenant.
- cache_hit_ratio_by_tenant: ratio (hits/requests) calculated at minute granularity; report p50/p90/p99 over 1h windows. Critical for SLOs.
- tail_latency_token_ms: histogram aggregated per 1s bucket; compute p50/p95/p99 per model and route.
- dashboard_query_cost_hourly: derived meter from billing logs; unit=USD/hour (or query units) per dashboard_id and per panel_id.

Trace span naming conventions (suggested minimal):
- service: inference-runtime
- span name patterns:
   - request.receive (entry)
   - routing.lookup (policy evaluation)
   - model.load (cold vs warm tag)
   - kvcache.probe (tag: prefix, hit=true)
   - generate.tokens (annotate token_count, seq_len)
   - tool.call.compact (if collapsed)
- When sampling: ensure at least request.receive + routing.lookup + generate.tokens remain for errorful traces.

Dashboard quick sketches and editing rules:
- Rule: every heavy panel must display a small cost estimate in the corner (query_cost_last_24h).
- Rule: panels that aggregate high-cardinality labels must have a default rollup mode (topN) and an ephemeral drilldown to prevent expensive auto-refresh.
- Quick sketch: "Latency Investigator" panel: panel 1 = latency rollup by bucket (top10 models); panel 2 = small heatmap for hourly tail latency; panel 3 = on-demand tenant list (runs only when clicked); panel 4 = related recent traces sample (controlled by sampling flag).

Measurement plan and dashboards to track experiments:
- Canary dashboard for experiments: include these panels
   - experiment_id, start_time, owner
   - baseline_query_cost (last 14d) vs treatment_query_cost
   - key metrics (cache_hit_ratio, tail_latency, traces_ingested)
   - operator feedback log (short free-text entries)
- Use daily cron job to export experiment metrics to a lightweight sheet for quick comparison.

Rollout checklist (per experiment):
- [ ] Write experiment spec + owner + duration in this doc
- [ ] Add feature flag and default to off
- [ ] Deploy sampling / panel change behind flag
- [ ] Run for at least 14 days or until statistically significant (t-test or bootstrap on cost reduction)
- [ ] Run regression probes (seeded failure tests) to confirm no loss of detection
- [ ] Document outcome and next steps (promote, tweak, rollback)

Open questions / risks:
- How to maintain SLA for downstream customers who rely on full traces for debugging long tail output-quality regressions? (mitigation: keep targeted full-trace sampling for customers flagged by our quality-monitoring system)
- Do we have enough tagging consistency to safely collapse spans across services? (mitigation: add a lightweight span-version tag and a trace schema validator for PRs)
- Regulatory/Phi risk for traces in private deployments — must coordinate with privacy team before sampling changes there.

Next immediate actions (owner assignments):
- Lina: implement experiment #1 flag and small dashboard (due 2024-08-28)
- Omar: prototype span-collapser + unit tests (due 2024-09-07)
- Priya: create canary experiment dashboard and cost exporter (due 2024-09-03)

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add small SQL snippets for query_cost_hourly extraction (billing table) and attach to the confluence page.
- Add a short playbook snippet for on-call to opt a tenant into full-trace mode when investigating.
- Run tabletop with SREs to validate incident workflows when sampling is on.

Appendix (examples / quick SQL sketches):
- billing extraction (pseudo-SQL):
  SELECT dashboard_id, panel_id, SUM(cost_usd) as cost_24h
  FROM telemetry.billing_panel_cost
  WHERE ts > now()-interval '24 hours' AND panel_id in (list)
  GROUP BY dashboard_id, panel_id;

- sample rate check (pseudo-SQL):
  SELECT hour_bucket, count(*) as traces, SUM(CASE WHEN sample_flag=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as sampled_traces
  FROM telemetry.traces
  WHERE service='inference-runtime' AND ts > now()-interval '7 days'
  GROUP BY hour_bucket;

End of doc.
